'''Richard A. Muller''' (born January 6, 1944) is an American physicist and [[emeritus]] professor of physics at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. He was also a faculty senior scientist at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]. In early 2010, Muller and his daughter Elizabeth Muller founded the group ''[[Berkeley Earth]]'', an independent 501(c)(3) non-profit aimed at addressing some of the major concerns of the [[climate change skeptics]], in particular the [[global surface temperature]] record. In 2016, Richard and Elizabeth Muller co-founded Deep Isolation, a private company seeking to dispose of nuclear waste in [[Deep borehole disposal|deep boreholes.]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clifford |first=Catherine |date=2022-04-04 |title=This daughter and father founded a company to bury nuclear waste by drilling deep boreholes |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2022/04/04/deep-isolation-aims-to-bury-nuclear-waste-using-boreholes.html |access-date=2022-04-22 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life, education and career==
Muller, who grew up in the South [[The Bronx|Bronx]], attended public schools in New York City, including PS 65 (on 141st St), Junior High School 22 (on 167th St), and [[the Bronx High School of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Who is Richard Muller? - Quora|url = https://www.quora.com/Who-is-Richard-Muller|website = www.quora.com|access-date = 2016-01-10}}</ref> Muller obtained an [[Bachelor of Arts|A.B.]] degree at [[Columbia University]] ([[New York City|New York]]) and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] degree in [[physics]] from University of California, Berkeley. Muller began his career as a graduate student under [[Nobel Prize in Physics|Nobel laureate]] [[Luis Walter Alvarez|Luis Alvarez]] performing [[particle physics]] experiments and working with [[bubble chamber]]s.  During his early years he also helped to co-create [[accelerator mass spectrometry]] and made some of the first measurements of [[anisotropy]] in the [[cosmic microwave background]].

Subsequently, Muller branched out into other areas of science, and in particular the [[Earth science]]s.  His work has included attempting to understand the [[ice age]]s, dynamics at the [[core-mantle boundary]], patterns of [[extinction]] and [[biodiversity]] through time, and the processes associated with [[impact event|impact cratering]].  One of his most well known proposals is the [[Nemesis (hypothetical star)|Nemesis hypothesis]] suggesting the [[Sun]] could have an as yet undetected companion [[dwarf star]], whose perturbations of the [[Oort cloud]] and subsequent effects on the flux of [[comet]]s entering the [[Solar System#Inner Solar System|inner Solar System]] could explain an apparent 26 million year periodicity in [[extinction event]]s.

In March 2011, he testified to the [[U.S. House Science, Space and Technology Committee]] that preliminary data confirmed an overall [[global warming]] trend.<ref>Lauren Morello, [https://www.nytimes.com/gwire/2011/03/31/31greenwire-study-of-temperature-data-confirms-warming-tre-84356.html?scp=4&sq=Richard%20Muller&st=cse "Study of Temperature Data Confirms Warming Trend, Scientist Tells House Panel"], The New York Times, March 31, 2011.</ref> On July 28, 2012, he stated, "Humans are almost entirely the cause."<ref name=NYTOpEd>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/07/30/opinion/the-conversion-of-a-climate-change-skeptic.html|work=[[New York Times]]|date=July 30, 2012|title=The conversion of a climate change skeptic|first=Richard A.|last=Muller}}</ref>

Along with [[Carl Pennypacker]],<ref>{{cite conference | title = The Acceleration of the Expansion of the Universe: A Brief Early History of the Supernova Cosmology Project (SCP) | first = Gerson | last = Goldhaber | date = February 20, 2008 | conference = Dark Matter 2008 | location = [[Marina del Rey, California]] | pages = 53&ndash;72}}</ref> Muller started The Berkeley Real Time Supernova Search,<ref>{{cite conference | title = The Status of Berkeley's Realtime Supernova Search | last1 = Perlmutter | first1 = Saul  | last2 = Crawford | first2 = Frank S.  | last3 = Muller | first3 = Richard A.  | last4 = Sasseen | first4 = Timothy P.  | last5 = Pennypacker | first5 = Carlton R. | last6 = Smith | first6 = Craig K.  | last7 = Treffers | first7 = R.  | last8 = Williams | first8 = R.  | date = July 13–24, 1987 | conference = The Ninth Santa Cruz Summer Workshop in Astronomy and Astrophysics | editor = Robinson, L.B.  | book-title = Instrumentation for Ground-Based Optical Astronomy, Present and Future | publisher = [[Springer-Verlag]] | location = Lick Observatory | page = 674 | isbn = 0-387-96730-3 | bibcode = 1988igbo.conf..674P }}</ref> which became The Berkeley Automated Supernova Search.<ref>{{cite conference | title = A doubly robotic telescope - The Berkeley Automated Supernova Search | last1 = Perlmutter | first1 = Saul | last2 = Muller | first2 = Richard A.  | last3 = Newberg | first3 = Heidi J. M.  | last4 = Pennypacker | first4 = Carlton R.  | last5 = Sasseen | first5 = Timothy P.  | last6 = Smith | first6 = Craig K.  | date = June 22–24, 1991 | conference = 103rd Annual Meeting of the Astronomical Society of the Pacific | book-title = Robotic telescopes in the 1990s | location =[[University of Wyoming]], Laramie | pages = 67&ndash;71 | bibcode = 1992ASPC...34...67P}}</ref>  It then became the [[Supernova Cosmology Project]], which discovered the [[accelerating expansion of the universe]], for which Muller's graduate student, [[Saul Perlmutter]], shared the 2011 [[Nobel Prize in Physics]].

==Positions and recognition==
In the 1980s, Muller joined the [[JASON (advisory group)|JASON]] advisory group, which brings together prominent scientists as consultants for the [[United States Department of Defense]].<ref>{{cite book|url=http://ulmo.ucmerced.edu/pdffiles/gmacdonald.pdf|title=Gordon James Fraser MacDonald, 1930-2002: A Biographical Memoir|author1=Walter Munk |author2=Naomi Oreskes |author2-link=Naomi Oreskes |author3=Richard Muller  |name-list-style=amp |publisher=National Academy of Sciences|date=2004|volume=84}}</ref>

He was named a [[MacArthur Foundation]] [[MacArthur Fellows Program#1982|Fellow in 1982]].  He also received the [[Alan T. Waterman Award]] in 1978 from the [[National Science Foundation]] "for highly original and innovative research which has led to important discoveries and inventions in diverse areas of physics, including astrophysics, [[radioisotope dating]], and optics".

Muller is a founder and board member of [[Berkeley Earth]], a non-profit organization focused on publishing independent analyses of the Earth's [[surface temperature record]]s.

In 1999, he received a distinguished teaching award from UC Berkeley.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.berkeley.edu/news/berkeleyan/1999/0414/awards_muller.html
|title=Distinguished Teaching Awards - Richard Muller
|work=The Berkeleyan
|publisher=UC Berkeley Office of Public Affairs|author=Steve Tollefson
|date=1999-04-14
|access-date=2011-03-01 }}</ref> His "Physics for Future Presidents" series of lectures, in which Muller teaches a synopsis of modern qualitative (i.e. without resorting to complicated math) physics, has been [https://www.youtube.com/view_play_list?p=095393D5B42B2266 released publicly] on [[YouTube]] by [[UC Berkeley]] and has been published in book form. It has been one of the most highly regarded courses at Berkeley. In December 2009, Muller officially retired from teaching the course, although he still occasionally gives guest lectures.

In 2015 a team including Muller received the [[Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics]] for the [[Supernova Cosmology Project]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://breakthroughprize.org/News/21 |title=Recipients Of The 2015 Breakthrough Prizes In Fundamental Physics And Life Sciences Announced |publisher=[[Breakthrough Prize]]|access-date=July 11, 2020}}</ref>

==MIT ''Technology Review''==
For several years, he was a monthly columnist with [[MIT]]'s ''[[Technology Review]]''.  In his August 2003 column on the [[polygraph]] machine used in lie detection examinations, Muller asserted that "the polygraph procedure has an accuracy between 80 and 95 percent".<ref>[https://www.technologyreview.com/2003/08/15/234130/when-lie-detectors-lie-or-dont/ "When Lie Detectors Lie or Don't," ''Technology Review,'' August 2003]</ref> The [[National Academy of Sciences, USA|National Academy of Sciences]] found that there is "little basis for the expectation that a polygraph test could have extremely high accuracy".<ref>[http://www.nap.edu/openbook.php?record_id=10420&page=212 “The Polygraph and Lie Detection”, ''National Academy of Sciences,'' 2003]</ref>

In his April 2002 column on the [[anthrax attacks]], Muller claimed "I think it likely that the anthrax terrorists were working for Osama bin Laden, and intended to murder thousands of people."<ref>[https://www.technologyreview.com/s/401419/al-qaedas-anthrax/ "Al Qaeda's Anthrax Is Osama bin Laden behind the mail attacks?" ''Technology Review,'' April 2002]</ref>

==Climate change==
===Hockey stick graph===
After the [[Soon and Baliunas controversy]] led to the paper being dismissed as defective and resignations of the journal's editors, Muller wrote in his 17 December 2003 ''[[Technology Review]]'' column that, while poor papers were not uncommon, Soon and Baliunas had attracted unusual attention for their portrayal of a prominent [[Medieval Warm Period]] in contrast to the [[Michael E. Mann|Mann]], [[Raymond S. Bradley|Bradley]] and [[Malcolm K. Hughes|Hughes]] (MBH99) reconstruction of the [[temperature record of the past 1000 years]]. This reconstruction, nicknamed the [[hockey stick graph (global temperature)|hockey stick graph]], had featured prominently in the [[IPCC Third Assessment Report]], and differed significantly from the schematic diagram shown in the [[IPCC First Assessment Report]]. Muller gave his views on the subsequent controversy. He noted the October 2003 paper by [[Stephen McIntyre]] and [[Ross McKitrick]] published in ''[[Energy and Environment]]'' which alleged that correction of errors in MBH99 would show a strong medieval warm period, and said this paper raised pertinent questions.<ref name="muller03">{{Cite web  | last = Muller | first = Richard | title = Medieval Global Warming | url = http://muller.lbl.gov/TRessays/23-MedievalGlobalWarming.html | publisher = [[Technology Review]] | access-date = 4 February 2013 }}</ref>

In an October 2004 ''Technology Review'' article, Muller discussed blog postings by McIntyre and McKitrick alleging that Mann, Bradley and Hughes did not do proper [[principal component analysis]] (PCA).<ref name=Bombshell>{{cite web |first=Richard |last=Muller |title=Global Warming Bombshell |url=https://www.technologyreview.com/2004/10/15/274740/global-warming-bombshell/ |publisher=[[Technology Review]]|date=October 15, 2004 |access-date=December 8, 2021}}</ref> In the article, Richard Muller stated:
<blockquote>
McIntyre and McKitrick obtained part of the program that Mann used, and they found serious problems. Not only does the program not do conventional PCA, but it handles data normalization in a way that can only be described as mistaken.

Now comes the real shocker. This improper normalization procedure tends to emphasize any data that do have the hockey stick shape, and to suppress all data that do not. To demonstrate this effect, McIntyre and McKitrick created some meaningless test data that had, on average, no trends. This method of generating random data is called "Monte Carlo" analysis, after the famous casino, and it is widely used in statistical analysis to test procedures. When McIntyre and McKitrick fed these random data into the Mann procedure, out popped a hockey stick shape!

That discovery hit me like a bombshell, and I suspect it is having the same effect on many others. Suddenly the hockey stick, the poster-child of the global warming community, turns out to be an artifact of poor mathematics. How could it happen?<ref name=Bombshell/>
</blockquote>
He went on to state "If you are concerned about global warming (as I am) and think that [[Human impact on the environment|human-created]] carbon dioxide may contribute (as I do), then you still should agree that we are much better off having broken the hockey stick. Misinformation can do real harm, because it distorts predictions."<ref name=Bombshell/> 
In an article on the [[RealClimate]] blog on various myths about the graph, Mann mentioned Muller's article as parroting the claims of McIntyre and McKitrick.<ref>Mann, Michael E., "[http://www.realclimate.org/index.php/archives/2004/12/myths-vs-fact-regarding-the-hockey-stick Myth vs fact regarding the 'Hockey Stick'], [[RealClimate]] (blog), 4 December 2004.</ref> Muller's opinion piece in the reputable MIT journal helped to spread the idea that the hockey stick shape was a statistical artifact, but several peer reviewed studies showed that the PCA methodology had little effect on the shape of the graph.<ref>{{citation
 |last1= Mann |first1= Michael E.
 |date= 6 March 2012 
 |title= The Hockey Stick and the Climate Wars: Dispatches from the Front Lines 
 |publisher= [[Columbia University Press]] 
 |isbn= 978-0-231-15254-9  
 |page= 140
}}</ref><ref name="AR4 WGI Chapter 6: Palaeoclimate">{{cite web | title=6.6 The Last 2,000 Years | website=AR4 WGI Chapter 6: Palaeoclimate | url=http://www.ipcc.ch/publications_and_data/ar4/wg1/en/ch6s6-6.html | access-date=16 March 2015 | archive-date=28 March 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150328093747/http://www.ipcc.ch/publications_and_data/ar4/wg1/en/ch6s6-6.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> By 2006 there was general acceptance of the conclusion of the graph that recent warming was unprecedented in 1,000 years.<ref name="Weart">{{cite web  |last= Weart |first= Spencer | author-link=Spencer R. Weart|title=Climate over Millennia (Hockey Stick graph) | website=American Institute of Physics | url=http://www.aip.org/history/climate/xmillenia.htm |date= December 2009| access-date=March 16, 2015}}</ref>

===Berkeley Earth===
In October 2011, Muller wrote in an op-ed in ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'', concerning his work with the [[Berkeley Earth Surface Temperature]] project:
<blockquote>
When we began our study, we felt that skeptics had raised legitimate issues, and we didn't know what we'd find. Our results turned out to be close to those published by prior groups. We think that means that those groups had truly been very careful in their work, despite their inability to convince some skeptics of that. They managed to avoid bias in their data selection, homogenization and other corrections.

Global warming is real. Perhaps our results will help cool this portion of the climate debate. How much of the warming is due to humans and what will be the likely effects? We made no independent assessment of that.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052970204422404576594872796327348|title=The Case Against Global-Warming Skepticism |publisher=[[Wall Street Journal]]|date=October 11, 2011}}</ref></p>
</blockquote>

While the BEST project did not delve into the proxy data sets used in the "hockey stick", the importance of the work regarding the modern temperature record is explained on the BEST web site:
<blockquote>
Existing data used to show global warming have met with much criticism. The Berkeley Earth project attempts to resolve current criticism of the former temperature analyses by making available an open record to enable rapid response to further criticism and suggestions. Our results include our best estimate for the global temperature change and our estimates of the uncertainties in the record.<ref>{{cite web |title=Why is the work being done by Berkeley Earth important? |url=http://berkeleyearth.org/FAQ.php#importance |publisher=[[Berkeley Earth Surface Temperature]] |year=2011 |access-date=March 17, 2012 |archive-date=July 20, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720061513/http://berkeleyearth.org/FAQ.php#importance |url-status=dead }}</ref>
</blockquote>

On July 28, 2012, he stated, "[G]lobal warming [is] real .... Humans are almost entirely the cause."<ref name=NYTOpEd/>

''[[Foreign Policy (magazine)|Foreign Policy]]'' named Muller one of its 2012 FP Top 100 Global Thinkers "for changing their minds".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://foreignpolicy.com/articles/2012/11/26/the_fp_100_global_thinkers?page=0,10#thinker10 |title=The FP Top 100 Global Thinkers |date=26 November 2012 |work=[[Foreign Policy]] |access-date=28 November 2012 |archive-date=30 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121130221322/http://www.foreignpolicy.com/articles/2012/11/26/the_fp_100_global_thinkers?page=0,33#thinker10 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Trends in tornado activity ===
In November 2013 Muller wrote an op-ed in ''[[The New York Times]]'' arguing that strong to violent [[tornado]] activity decreased since the 1950s and suggesting that [[global warming]] is the cause. Atmospheric scientists [[Paul Markowski (meteorologist)|Paul Markowski]], [[Harold E. Brooks]], et al., replied that Muller made substantial methodological flaws and was ignorant of long established findings in severe storms meteorology. They argue that there is no discernible decrease in significant tornado activity and that attribution of tornadic activity to global warming is premature although changes, especially in regional character, are likely as the atmospheric environment changes.<ref>{{cite news |last = Revkin |first = Andrew C. |title = A Closer Look at Tornadoes in a Human-Heated Climate |newspaper = The New York Times |date = 9 December 2013 |url = http://dotearth.blogs.nytimes.com/2013/12/09/a-closer-look-at-tornadoes-and-global-warming/ |access-date = 2014-02-20 }}</ref>

==Shale gas and hydraulic fracturing==
In a report for the [[Centre for Policy Studies]], Muller (and Elizabeth Muller of [[Berkeley Earth]], his daughter) wrote that the benefits of [[shale gas]], displacing harmful air pollution from coal, far outweigh the environmental costs of [[hydraulic fracturing|fracking]]. According to the Mullers, air pollution, mostly from coal burning, kills over three million people each year, primarily in the developing world. The Mullers state that "Environmentalists who oppose the development of shale gas and fracking are making a tragic mistake."<ref>[http://www.cps.org.uk/files/reports/original/131202135150-WhyEverySeriousEnvironmentalistShouldFavourFracking.pdf Why Every Serious Environmentalist Should Favour Fracking] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170712083322/http://www.cps.org.uk/files/reports/original/131202135150-WhyEverySeriousEnvironmentalistShouldFavourFracking.pdf |date=2017-07-12 }}, 2013 report</ref>

==Other work==
[[File:Muller Van de Graaff generator demonstration.jpg|thumb|Muller demos a [[Van de Graaff generator]]]]

Muller is President and Chief Scientist of Muller & Associates, an international consulting group specializing in [[energy]]-related issues.

Muller is Chief Technology Officer of SoliDDD Corp., which uses advanced optical design methods to deliver improved 3D images.<ref>[http://www.soliDDD.com SoliDDD Corp. home page]</ref>

Muller is co-founder and Chief Science Officer of Deep Isolation, a company offering [[Horizontal drillhole disposal|deep borehole disposal]] of nuclear waste.

Muller is co-founder and Chief Technology Officer of [[Deep Fission, Inc.]], a company developing an underground reactor concept it calls the [[Gravity Reactor]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Acclaimed Physicist And His Daughter Are Burying Tiny Nuclear Reactors A Mile Underground |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/christopherhelman/2026/04/02/acclaimed-physicist-and-his-daughter-are-burying-tiny-nuclear-reactors-a-mile-underground/ |publisher=Forbes |access-date=8 August 2026}}</ref>
